def: A rule in the agent harness that allows, asks about or denies a given tool call before it runs.
An enforced boundary, applied by the operating system, a hypervisor or a proxy, around running code that limits what it can reach.
Giving a component only the access its task requires, for an agent across files, commands, network, credentials and resources.
Layering independent controls so that a failure of one, such as a permission rule with a hole, does not defeat the system.
A process with a restricted view of the system built from namespaces, control groups and syscall filters, sharing the host kernel.
A user-space application kernel that handles a program's system calls itself instead of passing them to the host kernel.
A lightweight virtual machine with its own guest kernel, such as those run by Firecracker, that boots in well under a second.
A server outside the sandbox through which all outbound requests pass, deciding by allow-list which hosts may be contacted.
A default-deny list of hosts an agent may contact, matched on whole host labels and checked against the resolved address.
The tendency of people to approve prompts without reading them when prompts are frequent, which defeats confirmation as a control.
The macOS and Linux operating-system facilities used to start a process with file-system and network restrictions it cannot lift.
